events.title: United States Takes Possession of Alaska
events.description: In a formal ceremony at Sitka, Russia transferred Alaska to the United States following the purchase agreement signed in March 1867 for $7.2 million. The Russian flag was lowered and the American flag raised.
events.significance: The acquisition added about 586,000 square miles to the United States, giving it vast natural resources including gold, oil, and fisheries, and extending American strategic reach into the Arctic and Pacific.

events.title: British Broadcasting Company Founded
events.description: The British Broadcasting Company was formed by a consortium of wireless manufacturers to provide radio broadcasting services in the United Kingdom. It later became the publicly owned British Broadcasting Corporation in 1927.
events.significance: The BBC became one of the world's most influential public service broadcasters, setting standards for radio and television and shaping broadcasting models worldwide.

events.title: Death of Thomas Edison
events.description: American inventor and businessman Thomas Alva Edison died at his home in West Orange, New Jersey, at the age of 84. He held more than 1,000 US patents, including improvements to the phonograph, motion picture camera, and practical incandescent light bulb.
events.significance: Edison's work, including the establishment of the first industrial research laboratory, helped usher in the modern electrified world and the systematic approach to technological innovation.

events.title: United States Raises Flag Over Puerto Rico
events.description: Following the Spanish-American War, American forces formally took control of Puerto Rico on October 18, 1898, as Spanish sovereignty ended on the island. The transfer was later formalized by the Treaty of Paris.
events.significance: The change in sovereignty began Puerto Rico's long relationship with the United States as a territory, shaping its political status, citizenship, and economy to the present day.

events.title: West Side Story Film Premieres
events.description: The film adaptation of the Broadway musical West Side Story premiered in New York City, directed by Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins, with music by Leonard Bernstein and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim.
events.significance: The film won 10 Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and became a landmark of American musical cinema, influencing choreography, film musicals, and popular culture.
